items.title: Pulau Perhentian residents brace for Northeast Monsoon Floods
items.summary: JERTIH: Residents in the village on Pulau Perhentian here have started making early preparations for the Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to bring heavy rain and pose a flood risk to low-lying areas of the village. Resident Azizah Ab Rahman, 59, said the village was also vulnerable to flooding, especially when heavy rain coincided with high tides, causing water to stagnate and making it difficult for it to drain into the sea. Pulau Perhentian Village Development and Security Committee (JPKK) chairman Nik Zawawi Mohd Nor said about 30 houses were usually affected whenever flooding occurred in the village.

items.title: Zahid urges public to stay alert as northeast monsoon begins today
items.summary: He said the monsoon, expected to persist until March 2027, could bring prolonged heavy rainfall, flooding and rough seas, threatening residents’ safety, particularly in vulnerable areas. “This could increase the risk of flooding, particularly in areas near rivers and low-lying areas,” he said in a Facebook post today. Ahmad Zahid said strong winds during the period could also cause rough seas and rising sea levels in the South China Sea.

items.title: Meghan on TV menu for 'Junior MasterChef Australia'
items.summary: SYDNEY: Prince Harry's wife Meghan says she has agreed to feature as a special guest in television cooking sensation "Junior MasterChef Australia." Meghan, who was a guest judge on "MasterChef Australia" this year, is to appear in next year's contest for young cooks on Network 10. Harry, the second son of King Charles III and estranged brother of heir to the throne Prince William, married Meghan, an American former actor, at Windsor Castle in May 2018.

items.title: Israel to give verdict on Netanyahu in pivotal election
items.summary: JERUSALEM: A deeply divided Israel will head to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country's rightward drift. The last polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel's longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent. Netanyahu, 77, has served as Israel's prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.

items.title: USTR Greer tells EU that loan to Airbus threatens trade truce on aircraft financing
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US Trade Representative (USTR) Jamieson Greer told the European Union on Monday that a lack of information about its record-breaking loan to Airbus threatens a delicate transatlantic trade truce, including on financing large civil aircraft (LCA) projects. US planemaker Boeing had asked the US government in July to press for transparency on the loan, which came amid speculation that Airbus would use the funds to develop a new aircraft model. "This situation injects substantial uncertainty into transatlantic trade in the aerospace sector," Greer said.

items.title: Waze alternatives? Delivery riders, e-hailing drivers wait for TuJu to prove itself
items.summary: Muhammad Nabil Khairuddin, 30, a Grab rider, said he first learnt about TuJu through TikTok and Facebook yesterday and was considering downloading it to see how it compared with established navigation apps. For deliveries, however, Nabil said he already relied on Grab’s in-house navigation system, which allows him to find destinations without leaving the ride-hailing app. He said Grab previously allowed riders to choose between Waze and Google Maps, but its own navigation system now offered a more convenient option.

items.title: Fresher air in Malaysia again: Only Samalaju in Sarawak still unhealthy after months of haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Malaysia is breathing easier today, with only one place in the country still recording unhealthy air after a haze season that began in August. Banting (45) and Kuala Selangor (47) were rated “good”, while Petaling Jaya (52), Shah Alam (54), Klang (58) and Johan Setia (66) were moderate. Putrajaya recorded 54, while Cheras read 58 and Batu Muda 84 — the highest of the Klang Valley readings.

items.title: The Pacific and HIV: A chance to turn the tide — Eamonn Murphy, Saia Ma’u Piukala, Pio Smith, Beate Trankmann and Delphine Schantz
items.summary: For the Pacific, with its long tradition of collective action in tackling shared challenges, those hard-won lessons could help prevent today’s growing HIV epidemics from becoming a much larger crisis. The recent surge of international attention to Fiji’s HIV epidemic has carried uncomfortable echoes of an earlier era of AIDS. Papua New Guinea remains the largest HIV epidemic in the region, with an estimated 110,000 people living with HIV.

items.title: Asian stocks surge as Anthropic IPO lifts sentiment ahead of earnings, central banks
items.summary: SINGAPORE: Asian stocks surged on Tuesday as AI bellwether Anthropic's eagerly anticipated IPO filing lifted risk appetite ahead of tech earnings that will be a test for the AI trade, and central bank meetings that will influence near-term interest rates. Nasdaq futures was up 0.4 per cent after US chip stocks rose 2.8 per cent in overnight trade, clocking its biggest one-day jump in a month. European stock futures dipped 0.23 per cent.

items.title: Nancy Shukri warns withholding money for basic needs can amount to domestic abuse, urges victims to seek help
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — Being denied money for clothing, reprimanded over online purchases or forced to rely entirely on a partner for personal needs are among the situations that may constitute economic abuse within a household. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said domestic violence extended beyond physical and emotional abuse to include economic control, which could affect a victim’s well-being and self-confidence. She said this form of abuse warranted attention as it could occur in everyday situations, such as when a partner failed to provide money for basic family necessities or controlled personal spending, leaving the victim without financial autonomy.

items.title: Super El Nino: Ministry boosts food security measures
items.summary: Its minister, Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu, said the agrofood sector faces mounting challenges from the Middle East conflict alongside extreme heat and prolonged dry weather, which could disrupt staple food supplies. He said close monitoring is focused on dam water levels, particularly Kedah's Ahning Dam, where levels remain at alert and warning thresholds, threatening padi cultivation across the Muda granary area. Mohamad said preparations were also under way in the fisheries sector, as rising sea temperatures shift fish distribution, affect aquaculture water quality, and threaten reef ecosystems.

items.title: Durian orchard that never was: CEO to face charge over RM1.65m scam in Shah Alam court today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The chief executive officer of a fruit and vegetable wholesale, import and export company is expected to be charged today over a durian orchard purchase scam involving about RM1.65 million, the New Straits Times reported. MACC chief Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest. The MACC previously launched Op Kingfruit over a durian investment scam in Raub, Pahang, freezing bank accounts and seizing assets worth RM16.15 million.

items.title: Study on National Disaster Management Bill to be completed within 12 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A baseline study on the proposed Disaster Risk Reduction Act, following the proposal for the National Disaster Management Bill, is expected to be completed within 12 months. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the findings and recommendations of the study, conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), would be reviewed and coordinated with relevant ministries and agencies before the proposed policy and legislation are finalised. "At present, a specific timeline for the tabling of the National Disaster Management Bill in the Dewan Rakyat has yet to be determined.

items.title: Gold eases as stronger dollar weighs, Fed meeting in focus
items.summary: LONDON: Gold prices edged lower in early Asian trade on Tuesday as a firmer US dollar weighed on greenback-denominated bullion, while investors awaited Federal Reserve's policy meeting this week for clues on the interest-rate outlook. FUNDAMENTALS * Spot gold was down 0.1 per cent at $4,013.70 per ounce by 0045 GMT, while US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.3 per cent to $4,027.10. * Spot silver edged 0.1 per cent higher to US$53.97 per ounce, platinum steadied at US$1,527.81 and palladium slid 0.7 per cent to US$1,042.43.

items.title: TH traces funds to recover RM980m debt from Saudi firm
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said TH was pursuing recovery efforts with the relevant parties in Saudi Arabia. He said agreements signed between TH and Al-Rawda from 2014 to 2017 involved legacy lease investments, under which TH leased four hotels in Makkah and Madinah on a long-term basis. Zulkifli said Al-Rawda initiated arbitration proceedings against TH in 2021, resulting in an award ordering the company to pay TH SAR899 million (RM980 million).

items.title: Crowds throng Kelantan gold shops as prices fall to RM503 a gramme
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Gold prices falling to RM503 a gramme have drawn crowds to jewellery shops across Kelantan since yesterday. Customer Halima Osman, 45, said she was surprised by the sharp decline, as prices had previously approached RM600 a gramme. "Now that prices are low, we buy.

items.title: Govt compiling refugee data through registration programme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is collecting data on refugee communities nationwide through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the first phase focused on those held at immigration depots. He said the programme was expected to enter its second phase soon, covering holders of United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) cards outside the depots.

items.title: In Dewan Rakyat today: Health commission, hospital overcrowding and disaster risk mapping among key issues
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The proposed Health Services Commission, overcrowding at government hospitals and measures to strengthen disaster risk mapping in Malaysia are among the issues scheduled to be raised in the Dewan Rakyat today. According to the Order Paper published on Parliament’s website, Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa (PH-Sekijang) will ask the Health Minister to state the ministry’s commitment to tabling the proposed Health Services Commission Bill for first reading before the end of 2027, in line with the reform aspirations outlined in the 2023 Health White Paper. Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson) will seek an explanation from the Health Minister on persistent overcrowding at emergency departments, including average patient waiting times and concrete measures to ease congestion and ensure patients receive timely treatment.

items.title: STR, Sara should remain short term to help with rising living costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) assistance programmes must remain short-term measures rather than permanent features, as they are designed to help households cope with rising living costs and maintain their purchasing power, an economist said. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said continued reliance on such assistance could undermine the effectiveness of long-term government efforts in areas such as education, training, healthcare and infrastructure in promoting social mobility. He said government agencies should engage with communities to explain that the assistance is a temporary measure and encourage households to take advantage of government education and training programmes to improve their living standards.

items.title: Landslide victim Dr Wong helped couple realise 12-year dream of parenthood
items.summary: Dr Wong had served as an occupational health doctor (OHD) for decades, sharing his knowledge with OSH practitioners across Penang. He helped turn Azly and his wife's 12-year wait for a child into reality. Azly said he learnt in 2021 through a colleague that Dr Wong had a special interest in NaProTechnology, a natural fertility approach developed through the work of Dr Thomas W. Hilgers.

items.title: TuJu built for stranded motorists on expressways, not to rival Waze, says highway authority chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — TuJu was never meant to rival Waze, Malaysian Highway Authority chairman Datuk Seri Hasni Mohammad has said. His clarification comes after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim urged Malaysian civil servants to switch to the local app over security concerns linked to Waze’s Israeli ties. He said TuJu was conceived as an added service for tolled highway users, offering traffic updates, rest area details, enforcement camera locations and emergency contacts, stressing that its real value, Hasni said, lies when the vehicle breaks down.

items.title: Oil eases on Middle East diplomacy hopes, Saudi attacks keep supply worries alive
items.summary: LONDON: Oil prices edged lower on Tuesday as the potential for a resolution in the US-Israeli war on Iran kept supply fears at bay, but Brent stayed close to six-month highs as attacks on Saudi Arabia lowered hopes of immediate stability in the region. Brent crude futures were down 66 cents, or 0.57 per cent, at US$115.15 a barrel as of 0000 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 44 cents, or 0.43 per cent, at US$101.32. Brent prices touched US$117 on Monday as well.

items.title: Explainer: Are Malaysian-linked firms in trouble over Singapore's haze notices?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four companies with links to Malaysian-listed groups have been caught up in Singapore's efforts to tackle the haze that has lingered across the region for weeks. Which companies have Malaysian connections? Two are Singapore-incorporated subsidiaries of Bursa Malaysia-listed TSH Resources Bhd – TSH Global Plantation Pte Ltd and TSH Oversea Pte Ltd.

items.title: Two motorcyclists killed in three-vehicle crash on Johor Bahru-Gelang Patah road
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 27 — Two motorcyclists were killed in a collision involving three vehicles at Kilometre 24.9 of the Johor Bahru-Gelang Patah-Pendas Road here yesterday morning. Iskandar Puteri District Police Chief ACP Radin Ramlan Radin Taha said that at about 7.20 am, a car carrying a driver and two passengers was travelling towards Lima Kedai. “The bodies were sent to Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) in Johor Bahru for post-mortems, while the car driver and two passengers sustained minor injuries to their heads, faces and right legs,” he said in a statement tonight.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar, major currencies
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar and other major currencies on Tuesday as Malaysia's resilient economic fundamentals continued to support the local note amid lingering geopolitical risks in West Asia, an analyst said. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0840/0905 against the greenback from Tuesday's close of 4.0855/0895. © New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

items.title: Super El Nino threat: Govt steps up measures to protect padi supply, fisheries as heat and drought loom
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) has stepped up inter-agency preparedness measures to address the Super El Nino phenomenon, which is already showing early effects in the country. “These include implementing Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM), expanding the Smart Irrigation Monitoring System, introducing alternative water management methods for padi cultivation and promoting Controlled Environment Agriculture (CEA) to ensure sustainable water security,” he said when winding up debate on the Supply Bill 2027 for the ministry in the Dewan Rakyat yesterday. Mohamad said extensive preparations were also under way in the fisheries sector, as rising sea temperatures were altering fish distribution patterns, affecting aquaculture water quality and threatening reef ecosystems.

items.title: Penang Muda wants hillside project approvals revoked
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government must revoke all approvals for hillside development projects following a series of deadly landslides across the state. Penang Muda state committee member Andika Putera said local councils, particularly the Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Prai City Council (MBSP), must prioritise public safety and environmental sustainability over commercial interests. "Such projects only expose residents and workers to unnecessary risks," he said today.

items.title: #NSTviral: Viral clip of distressed vendor sparks debate over trading permits
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A video showing a distressed woman amid the scattered aftermath of an alleged enforcement action has gone viral on social media, sparking widespread discussions online. The video, uploaded by TikTok user @mrmamahome, captures the scene, with beverage containers, food items, and trading equipment strewn across the pavement. The clip has since drawn mixed reactions across social media platforms.

items.title: Democrats call for special counsel to probe Trump's Epstein ties
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Democratic lawmakers called on Monday, eight days before crucial US midterm elections, for the appointment of a special counsel to probe President Donald Trump's ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. "Five women have directly accused Trump of rape or sexual assault in Epstein's company or presence," Raskin said. The House Judiciary Committee Democrats called on Attorney General Todd Blanche to appoint an independent special counsel to investigate Trump's ties to Epstein.

items.title: Only Samalaju records unhealthy air quality this morning
items.summary: According to the Department of Environment's (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Samalaju recorded an API reading of 151. Another 42 areas recorded moderate API readings, including Bintulu, Serian, Sibu, Batu Muda, Kluang and Kuching. Meanwhile, 25 stations recorded good API readings, including Port Dickson, Limbang, Bandaraya Melaka, Tanah Merah and Kemaman.

items.title: Fire and Rescue Department mobilises 25,592 personnel, 1,248 assets ahead of Northeast Monsoon
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — A total of 25,592 officers and personnel of the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), along with 1,248 assets, are on standby to face the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), which is expected to begin tomorrow and last until March next year. JBPM director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the department had strengthened its operational planning by ensuring personnel availability, asset and logistical readiness, and the strategic deployment of resources to deal with possible disasters throughout the period. “In terms of personnel, JBPM’s preparedness plan includes 13,631 full-time fire officers (PSM), 2,227 Auxiliary Fire Officers (PBB), 8,956 Volunteer Fire Brigade (PBS) members and 62 engineering personnel.

items.title: Three men arrested after firefighter dies in Port Dickson hit-and-run, driver allegedly fled scene
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 27 — Police have arrested three local men to assist in investigations into a fatal accident involving a firefighter at KM2.6 of Jalan Pantai, Port Dickson, this morning. Port Dickson police chief, Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan, said that the three men, aged 31 and 32, comprised the driver of a Toyota Vios and two friends, who allegedly conspired to hide the car in Puchong, Selangor, and remove its registration number plates. Ahmad Afiq added that the car driver was subsequently arrested at the Serdang police headquarters at about 6.30 pm today, while his two friends were arrested in Puchong.

items.title: Fahmi: RM5b Jendela revamp to use Starlink, small cells to close Malaysia’s final 1pc Internet coverage gap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The National Digital Network (Jendela) initiative is being modified to use alternative technologies such as Starlink and small cells to achieve 100 per cent Internet coverage in populated areas, says Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzi. The goal is to ensure 100 per cent coverage in populated areas, including the most remote locations. Apart from remote settlements, Fahmi said the restructuring of the Jendela initiative also marked a paradigm shift from solely focusing on Coverage of Populated Areas (COPA) to Economic Area Coverage.

items.title: RM1.65mil durian orchard scam: CEO to be charged today
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A chief executive officer of a fruit and vegetable wholesale, import, and export company is expected to be charged in court today over a durian orchard purchase scam involving about RM1.65 million. A source said initial investigations revealed the suspect committed the offence in February 2024, but the purchase of the orchard never materialised. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest.

items.title: Johor Gleneagles Hospital expands university partnerships to nurture future nurses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Johor Gleneagles Hospital plans to expand its partnerships with universities and educational institutions to offer more sponsorship opportunities to students pursuing nursing careers. It said the initiative builds on the hospital's existing collaborations with Nilai University and Universiti Selangor (Unisel) under its Nursing Sponsorship Programme. Of these, 51 have graduated, with 17 already joining Johor Gleneagles Hospital.

items.title: Bukit Aman seizes RM765,750 in unregistered health products, suspected counterfeit goods in KL raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 —The Wildlife Crime Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) unit of Bukit Aman’s Internal Security and Public Order Department seized unregistered health and cosmetic products alongside suspected counterfeit branded goods worth RM765,750 during a raid on a courier company’s premises here this morning. He said the integrated operation resulted in the seizure of 9,257 units of health products, cosmetics, and branded goods suspected of violating statutory regulations. Mohd Zaki said further inspection uncovered 9,130 units of various brands of health and cosmetic products suspected of not being registered with MOH, as well as 127 branded items suspected of bearing counterfeit trademarks.

items.title: Britain will not join Canada-led defence bank initiative
items.summary: BENGALURU: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, in a setback to efforts to create the world's first global defence bank, according to a person familiar with the matter. "We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives," the statement said. The MDM will focus on accelerating defence investment, joint procurement through financing and bringing together demand across Nato allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defence industries and supply chains, with a greater focus on lending to individual sovereign states, the person added.

items.title: Bangladesh courts Malaysian tourists with tourism push
items.summary: Bangladesh High Commissioner to Malaysia Manjurul Karim Khan Chowdhury said stronger cooperation between the tourism industries could boost tourist arrivals and people-to-people exchanges. He said this at the Bangladesh Tourism Presentation at Wyndham Kuala Lumpur yesterday, which showcased the country's attractions, heritage and tourism infrastructure to Malaysian industry players. The event was organised by Travel Canvas with the support of the Bangladesh High Commission, Bangladesh Tourism Board (BTB) and Bangladesh-Malaysia Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BMCCI).

items.title: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate says court barred him from leaving country
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro said on Monday that the Supreme Court had ordered him to surrender his passports and barred him from leaving the country following his loss to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Sunday's run-off election, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Bolsonaro said Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes had issued the ruling on Sunday night, shortly after Lula was declared the winner. "I never thought about leaving the country," Bolsonaro said, adding that he would comply with the passport surrender order while challenging the ruling.

items.title: Tighter economics on Cress, but still viable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The new System Access Charge (SAC) under the Acceleration Package of the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (Cress) announced by the Energy and Water Transformation Ministry comes as a surprise to renewable energy developers (RED) and green consumers (GCs). Cypark Resources Bhd chief investment officer Belqaizi Taufik said that under the current Cress Acceleration Package, the economics are tighter than what the industry initially expected when 14 sen/kWh SAC was announced on Sept 18. However, the commercial case remains and Cress can still be competitive for large energy users, particularly data centres, said Belqaizi in a written response to Business Times' questions.

items.title: PH to highlight Anwar govt’s welfare aid and security record in Melaka election campaign, says Saifuddin
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 27 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) will implement a prudent campaign in the Melaka State Election (PRN) by explaining the Unity Government’s initiatives under the leadership of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to the rakyat. Home Minister and Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) Vice President Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the successes and welfare initiatives implemented by the government must be conveyed in the best possible way to voters so that they are confident in choosing candidates from PH. School uniforms, school shoes, sports attire, school bags, school supplies, insya-Allah, are covered.

items.title: Anwar: RM150m allocated to complete 554 Felda new-generation homes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government has allocated an additional RM150 million to complete three Felda New Generation Housing Projects (PGBF) involving 554 housing units. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the projects, comprising 200 units each at Felda Bukit Aping Timur and Felda Pasak, and 154 units at Felda Kerteh 5, were announced during Felda Settlers’ Day on July 7. On the Rumah Pahang housing project at Felda Jengka 11, he said it had been fully handed over to the Pahang government, specifically through the Pahang Housing and Property Board (LPHP).

items.title: Malaysia compiling nationwide refugee data under new registration programme, says Zahid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The government is compiling data on refugee communities nationwide through the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme under National Security Council (MKN) Directive No. 23, says Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. “At present, the government also requires UNHCR to facilitate third-country resettlement, as recipient nations rely on the UNHCR card to verify and authenticate refugees,” he said.

items.title: Disaster Risk Reduction Act study expected to be completed within 12 months
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 27 — The baseline study on the proposed Disaster Risk Reduction Act, following the proposal for the National Disaster Management Bill, is expected to be completed within 12 months. Deputy Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, said that the findings and recommendations of the study, conducted by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), would be reviewed and coordinated with the relevant ministries and agencies before the proposed policy and legislation were finalised. “At present, a specific timeline for the tabling of the National Disaster Management Bill in the Dewan Rakyat has yet to be determined.

items.title: Felda settler hacked to death with axe in Johor rampage
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 27 — A Felda settler was hacked to death with an axe in an alleged violent rampage at Felda Lok Heng Selatan here last night. Kota Tinggi police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said police were investigating the incident. He said police would issue an official statement on the incident today.

items.title: MGS could face renewed volatility as US Fed look at rates
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields and foreign fund flows could face renewed volatility following this week's US Federal Reserve meeting, as investors assess the implications of its policy outlook for global bond markets. Economist Professor Geoffrey Williams said a US rate increase could put some upward pressure on MGS yields, although the impact would likely be limited because Malaysian government bonds were predominantly held by domestic investors. "If those concerns drive US Treasury yields lower, MGS could benefit from improved relative value and renewed foreign interest," he said.

items.title: Trump offers US$1mil reward for voter fraud reports ahead of midterm elections
items.summary: WASHNIGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that he plans to pay US$1 million (RM4.09 million) to anyone reporting voter fraud in past elections or the upcoming midterm elections on Nov 3, provided the information leads to the arrest and conviction of those responsible, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid US$1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!" Trump said on Truth Social.

items.title: Denying spouse money may constitute domestic violence, says Nancy
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Being denied money for clothing, reprimanded over online purchases or forced to rely entirely on a partner for personal needs are among the situations that may constitute economic abuse within a household. Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said domestic violence extended beyond physical and emotional abuse to include economic control, which could affect a victim's well-being and self-confidence. She said this form of abuse warranted attention as it could occur in everyday situations, such as when a partner failed to provide money for basic family necessities or controlled personal spending, leaving the victim without financial autonomy.

items.title: Syria says at least six dead in Jordan strikes
items.summary: DAMASCUS: Syrian authorities said at least six people were killed in strikes on Monday in the country's south, as Jordan said it had targeted "terrorist organisations" after a deadly jihadist attack on a church. In an updated statement, health authorities in Daraa province reported "six martyrs, including three children and a woman", after earlier reporting eight victims. Syria's civil defence agency instead reported a total of seven people killed in several locations — six of them in Daraa province, including three children.

items.title: Want to plan your finances to have enough for retirement in Malaysia? Here are some tips
items.summary: In planning for your retirement finances, Rajen said you could split your net income (after paying taxes) into three portions of about 33 per cent each: Past (Money that you have already spent, but are paying now = Existing debts, e.g. If you are currently contributing 11 per cent to your EPF retirement savings, Rajen said this means you would need to put aside about another 22 per cent into sources that can generate passive income for the future. “They need to work harder, work longer, work smarter to increase their active income, their earned income.

items.title: Budget 2027 autism initiatives aim to bridge early education gap for rural, low-income children
items.summary: KUANTAN, Oct 27 — Access to appropriate early education and guidance is essential for autistic children, particularly those from low-income families and rural communities, to help them develop their potential early on. Against this backdrop, plans under Budget 2027 to build two Permata Kurnia centres in Pahang and Melaka and open 130 new Tabika Tunas Istimewa classes in rural areas nationwide are expected to give more children access to education and support suited to their individual needs. He said stronger cooperation among the government, experts, parents and childcare providers was essential to ensure autistic children received the support they needed for their development and well-being.

items.title: Nepal turns to SMART’s drones, detection gear after declining two Malaysian rescue offers
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — Malaysia’s third offer to assist Nepal in its search and rescue (SAR) operations for mud flood victims was accepted after two earlier offers were turned down, paving the way for the deployment of the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART), equipped with technical expertise and advanced detection equipment. SMART commander Senior Fire Superintendent 1 Abdul Manaf Che Isa, who led the mission, said Malaysia initially offered to send 50 rescuers, followed by a second offer of 25 personnel with SAR equipment, but Nepal declined both offers because it already had sufficient rescue teams. He said Nepal’s government eventually accepted Malaysia’s third offer, which involved deploying just 11 SMART personnel, nine high-capacity drones and specialised detection equipment, after several rounds of discussions.

items.title: Abang Johari confirms AI data centre plan in Sarawak under US$50b investment
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 26 — The US$50 billion investment announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim recently includes strategic plans by a major international company to develop an artificial intelligence (AI) data centre in Tanjung Embang. Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg said further details, including the name of the company involved, could not be disclosed at this stage to preserve the confidentiality of the corporate transaction. The Premier said the international technology giant had chosen Kuching as its investment destination because it viewed Sarawak as a forward-looking state that was aggressively transitioning towards a new economy.

items.title: Live pig imports from Sarawak to Selangor subject to strict controls since July 2025, says deputy minister
items.summary: He said Sarawak Minister of Food Industry, Commodity and Regional Development Datuk Seri Dr Stephen Rundi Utom had announced the matter in July 2025 during an official loading ceremony at Pending Port, Sarawak. Further clarification had also been provided by Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup, who was then Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister, and by Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu through oral question sessions and written replies in the Dewan Rakyat. Chan said Selangor Infrastructure and Agriculture Committee chairman Datuk Izham Hashim had also explained that the state government allowed the issuance of import licences for live pigs from Sarawak, subject to strict conditions and control procedures.

items.title: Court of Appeal slashes Klang council’s RM117m dumpsite damages bill to RM3m
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 26 — The Court of Appeal today reduced the damages payable by the Klang Municipal Council, now known as the Klang Royal City Council, to property developer NBC Land Sdn Bhd from RM117 million to RM3 million in a dispute over the rehabilitation of a former dumpsite. “The parties agreed to share this estimated cost of RM6 million equally, 50 percent each (RM3 million each),” he said. Therefore, he said the court substitute the High Court’s award with RM3 million in damages, representing the council’s agreed 50 per cent share of the RM6 million rehabilitation cost.

items.title: Zahid extends aid to two Bernama, NST journalists injured in Ipoh-Lumut road crash
items.summary: IPOH, Oct 26 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has extended financial assistance and words of encouragement to two journalists from the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and the New Straits Times (NST) who were injured in a road accident on the Ipoh-Lumut road yesterday. Speaking at Zahratulhayat’s residence in Klebang Harmoni, Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid had also pledged to monitor their recovery and provide further assistance where needed. Shuhaimi said Ahmad Zahid appreciated the solidarity and moral support shown by the Ipoh media fraternity towards the injured journalists.

items.title: Dewan Rakyat Speaker asks Rayer to write formally over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer has been asked to write an official letter to Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul if he wants Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Bharu) to be referred to the Parliament Rights and Privileges Committee. Johari said that the committee will examine the matter regarding Takiyuddin’s use of the word “hypocrite” (munafik), which was linked to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim during the debate on the 2027 Budget last Monday, before making any decision. Johari explained that he had previously asked Takiyuddin to retract the word, but the PAS Secretary-General, via a letter dated October 22, suggested that a mediation process be held without retracting the word.

items.title: Melaka schools to remain open amid haze, outdoor activities suspended if API exceeds 100
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — All educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) in Melaka will operate as usual tomorrow, said the Melaka State Education Department. In a statement, the Melaka Education Department announced that outdoor classroom activities may proceed as usual in areas recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading below 100. However, the department stated that all outdoor activities, including physical education, co-curricular and sports activities, camps, celebrations, assemblies, and activities in open halls, must be suspended if the API reading exceeds 100, in line with MOE Circular No.

items.title: Fuziah: PKR fields seven new faces among nine candidates for Melaka polls
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 26 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) is fielding seven new faces among its nine candidates in the upcoming Melaka state election, reflecting its push for leadership renewal. Its secretary-general Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the new faces make up 77.8 per cent of the party’s line-up, including four young candidates. She said three women are also among the candidates, accounting for 33.3 per cent of the party’s total.

items.title: British nationals top KLIA drug mule arrests, drugs worth RM202.76m seized
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 26 — A total of 77 cases linked to drug mule syndicates at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) were recorded between January and Oct 15, with 93 individuals arrested. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said these cases involved the seizure of 2,526.28 kilogrammes (kg) of drugs, with an estimated value of RM202.76 million. He said the seized substances comprised 2,407.27 kg of cannabis (64 cases), 77.837 kg of methamphetamine (four cases), 22.11 kg of ketamine (four cases), 15.585 kg of cocaine (three cases), and 3.475 kg of a mixture of ketamine and cannabis (two cases).
